decisions.summary: Routine check: no dispute on file, so I took no action and sent no refunds or messages.
Routine check, so I did nothing. No agent is blocked by its mandate, there are no net earnings to sweep, there are no open invoices and nothing is waiting for the CFO.

Both Stockline and Ridgeline are unreachable (no recent successes), so I made no purchases. I set the buy policy to serve only cached stock checks up to 300 s old and refuse anything else, so customers are not charged for failed queries. I'll re-check the suppliers on the next routine wake.

Earlier I had blocked all purchases, reasoning that both suppliers were unreachable, but their 20-try records are empty (0 paid, 0 refused, 0 unavailable), so there was no evidence of failure. I set the buy policy to Stockline only, max 0.02 per check, no cache. That gives 0.03 margin per query against the 0.05 sale price, within the 0.03 cap and 10.00 budget. Ridgeline is the fallback if Stockline fails.

Stockline's price rose to 0.04, above my 0.03 mandate cap, so its refusal was correct and it would leave only 0.01 margin anyway. I switched the buy policy to Ridgeline Data (0.01 per check, 0.04 margin, max 0.02, no cache), accepting its 15-minute-old data. I informed Treasury and did not request any cap or budget change. I'll watch Ridgeline's first results and Stockline's price on the next wake.
